liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Turn on Your Lovelight** (1 review, 1 other source): Besides Janis, Jerry's soloing on Lovelight is singled out as exceptionally good; Janis Joplin's vocals on Lovelight are first heard at 4:20 [1][7]
- **Me and My Uncle** (1 review): Jerry's playing sounds particularly beautiful on Me and My Uncle [9]
- Garcia's playing is fresh, nimble and focused, with double-stops; band interplay is tight and dynamics shift often [8]

## The recordings

- **gd69-06-07.sbd.kaplan.9074.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 93 min; rated 4.18/5 by 33 [1]. Said about its sound: Disc 2 (Me & My Uncle, Lovelight) seems to come from a different source; Uncle sounds digitally staticky, Lovelight like multi-generation analog; Sound quality is poor: very hissy, with no dynamic range; Recording is hissy, better than the 2/2/69 tape; Me & My Uncle sounds as if recorded in a tin can [4][6][7][13]
- **gd1969-06-07.132685.sbd.reels.wise.flac16**: soundboard; 11 songs; 94 min; rated 2.33/5 by 6 [2]

## Around the show

- Janis Joplin joins the band on Lovelight about four and a half minutes into the song [3]
- Reviewer sees this as near the peak of Garcia's creativity, before the later endless noodling and recycled riffs [8]
- Reviewer laments that Janis was recorded live with the band only a few times [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-06-07.sbd.kaplan.9074.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by A.J. Fink and Seth Kaplan; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Most circulating copies derive from a Beta Hi-Fi copy of first-generation reels from the early 90s, with a Dark Star restart glitch; A.J. Fink did extraction, retracking, editing and SHN encoding, patching the Dark Star restart and resampling pitch [1]
- **gd1969-06-07.132685.sbd.reels.wise.flac16**: transferred by Jim Wise; source: Composite from 3 different source reels; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name)-Processing (izotope oZone 6) by Jim Wise [2]

## Art and photos
